page: Microsoft Azure B2pts_v2 is a burstable, entry-tier virtual machine built on 64-bit ARM architecture. Powered by Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processors running at 3.0 GHz, the instance supplies 2 vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with one thread per core. Memory allocation is limited to 1.0 GB of RAM, equivalent to 0.5 GB per vCPU. The processor configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside native hardware acceleration for AES cryptography. The instance contains no dedicated GPU hardware and includes no local ephemeral storage, relying on external network-attached volumes for persistent data.

Performance benchmarks reflect the modest footprint and burstable credit model of the B2pts_v2. While single-core computational throughput is competitive for its class—scoring 1822.09 in stress-ng single-core tests—multi-core throughput registers at a weaker 3611.98 due to the constrained core count. Memory bandwidth achieves 27.09 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 16.47 GB/sec for writes, which contributes to lower benchmark tiers in comprehensive suites such as PassMark, where the CPU score reached 1605.25 and memory reached 829.4. Workload-specific tests yield 1.43 million operations per second for Redis SET operations and 1.55 GB/sec throughput for static web delivery.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the B2pts_v2 provides a resource-dense, low-overhead profile tailored for low-utilization scenarios. The Ampere ARM architecture delivers power-efficient compute, making the instance economical for non-continuous execution without paying for surplus resources. However, the 1.0 GB memory limit imposes a strict operational ceiling that makes it unsuitable for data caching, parallel builds, or concurrent services. The B2pts_v2 is strictly configured for lightweight microservices, monitoring probes, low-traffic edge web endpoints, test automation scripts, and background administrative jobs.
description: Microsoft Azure B2pts_v2 is an entry-level burstable instance powered by Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processors running at 3.0 GHz on the arm64 architecture. It provides 2 vCPUs across 2 physical cores, coupled with a constrained 1.0 GB memory pool (0.5 GB per vCPU), with no bundled GPU or local ephemeral storage. Benchmark testing shows average single-core CPU throughput via stress-ng (1822.09), alongside 27.09 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth and 1.55 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Overall multi-core and memory sub-scores reflect the tightly restricted memory capacity and burstable processing limits. The configuration delivers qualitative cost efficiency for intermittent, low-duty workloads where baseline execution suffices. It is best deployed for lightweight background automation, basic monitoring agents, low-traffic HTTP proxying, and minimal test environments that do not require high memory density or sustained CPU cycles.
